title: Troubleshooting Trap Seal Loss and Vent Blockages
description: Gurgling sounds in your sinks or foul sewer odors indoors often point to a compromised vent system rather than a direct drain clog. When a plumbing vent stack becomes restricted by debris, bird nests, or frost, discharging water creates a negative pressure vacuum. This siphon action pulls the protective water seal out of nearby P-traps, allowing sewer gases to escape into the building. Professional plumbers troubleshoot this by inspecting the vent terminal on the roof and checking for improper wet venting configurations inside walls.

Troubleshooting Trap Seal Loss and Vent Blockages

Gurgling sounds in your sinks or foul sewer odors indoors often point to a compromised vent system rather than a direct drain clog. When a plumbing vent stack becomes restricted by debris, bird nests, or frost, discharging water creates a negative pressure vacuum. This siphon action pulls the protective water seal out of nearby P-traps, allowing sewer gases to escape into the building. Professional plumbers troubleshoot this by inspecting the vent terminal on the roof and checking for improper wet venting configurations inside walls.
